5.277.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ye cānye bhāskarā statra saṃti brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yājñavalkyapratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 1 ..
5.277.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ये चान्ये भास्करा स्तत्र संति ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे याज्ञवल्क्यप्रतिष्ठिताः .. 1 ..
5.277.m: Sūta said: / And the other suns that are there, O best of brahmins, / in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, established by Yājñavalkya: 1

5.277.s:
yastānpūjayate bhaktyā hṛdi kṛtvā'bhivāṃchitān ..
saptamyāṃ caiva saptamyāṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 2 ..
5.277.d:
यस्तान्पूजयते भक्त्या हृदि कृत्वाऽभिवांछितान् ..
सप्तम्यां चैव सप्तम्यां लभते नात्र संशयः .. 2 ..
5.277.m: he who worships them with devotion, holding his desires in his heart, / on every seventh day [of the fortnight], obtains them; there is no doubt in this. 2

5.277.s:
.. ṛṣaya ucuḥ .. ..
eka eva sthitaḥ sūryo dṛśyate ca nabhastale ..
tatkathaṃ dvādaśaite ca tatra kṣetre pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
kasminkāle tathā kṛtye kimarthaṃ sūtanandana .. 3 ..
5.277.d:
.. ऋषय उचुः .. ..
एक एव स्थितः सूर्यो दृश्यते च नभस्तले ..
तत्कथं द्वादशैते च तत्र क्षेत्रे प्रतिष्ठिताः ..
कस्मिन्काले तथा कृत्ये किमर्थं सूतनन्दन .. 3 ..
5.277.m:
The seers said:
Only a single sun is seen staying in the sky. / How then were these twelve consecrated in that sacred field? / At what time, in what rite, and for what purpose, O son of Sūta? (3)

5.277.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
āsītpūrvaṃ kṛtirnāma śunaḥśepasamudbhavaḥ .. .. 4 ..
5.277.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
आसीत्पूर्वं कृतिर्नाम शुनःशेपसमुद्भवः .. .. 4 ..
5.277.m:
Sūta said:
Formerly, there was one named Kṛti, born from Śunaḥśepa. (4)

5.277.s:
tasya putraḥ śunaḥ putro babhūva munisattamaḥ ..
cārāyaṇaḥ sutastasya vabhūva munisattamaḥ .. 5 ..
5.277.d:
तस्य पुत्रः शुनः पुत्रो बभूव मुनिसत्तमः ..
चारायणः सुतस्तस्य वभूव मुनिसत्तमः .. 5 ..
5.277.m: His son was Śunaḥputra, best of sages; / his son was Cārāyaṇa, best of sages. (5)

5.277.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya brahmā loka pitāmahaḥ ..
sāvitrīśāpanirdagdho hyavatīrṇo dharātale .. 6 ..
5.277.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य ब्रह्मा लोक पितामहः ..
सावित्रीशापनिर्दग्धो ह्यवतीर्णो धरातले .. 6 ..
5.277.m: Then, after some time, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / burned by the curse of Sāvitrī, descended to the surface of the earth. (6)

5.277.s:
gāyatrī ca yadā viprāstenoḍhā yajñakarmaṇi ..
prāksthitāṃ ca parityajya sarvadevasamāgame ..
kālātyayo bhavennaiva sāvitryāgamane sthire .. 7 ..
5.277.d:
गायत्री च यदा विप्रास्तेनोढा यज्ञकर्मणि ..
प्राक्स्थितां च परित्यज्य सर्वदेवसमागमे ..
कालात्ययो भवेन्नैव सावित्र्यागमने स्थिरे .. 7 ..
5.277.m: When, O brahmins, Gāyatrī was taken by him as a wife in a sacrificial rite, / having set aside the one who stood before, in the assembly of all the gods, / so that there would be no lapse of proper time while the arrival of Sāvitrī was awaited, (7)

5.277.s:
tatastasya samādeśādgāyatrī gopakanyakā ..
śakreṇa ca samānītā divyalakṣaṇalakṣitā .. 8 ..
5.277.d:
ततस्तस्य समादेशाद्गायत्री गोपकन्यका ..
शक्रेण च समानीता दिव्यलक्षणलक्षिता .. 8 ..
5.277.m: then, by his command, the cowherd girl Gāyatrī, / endowed with divine marks, was brought there by Śakra. (8)

5.277.s:
gopakanyāṃ ca tāṃ jñātvā gośca vaktreṇa padmajaḥ ..
praveśyākarṣayāmāsa guhyena ca tataḥ param .. 9 ..
5.277.d:
गोपकन्यां च तां ज्ञात्वा गोश्च वक्त्रेण पद्मजः ..
प्रवेश्याकर्षयामास गुह्येन च ततः परम् .. 9 ..
5.277.m: And knowing her to be a cowherd girl, the lotus-born [Brahmā] made her enter through the mouth of a cow, / and pulled her out from its anus thereafter. (9)

5.277.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ caiva kulamekaṃ dvidhā sthitam ..
ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhaṃti havirekatra saṃsthitam .. 6.278.10 ..
5.277.d:
ब्राह्मणानां गवां चैव कुलमेकं द्विधा स्थितम् ..
एकत्र मन्त्रास्तिष्ठंति हविरेकत्र संस्थितम् .. 6.278.10 ..
5.277.m: For the lineage of brahmins and cows is one, divided in two: / in one place reside the mantras, in the other resides the oblation. (10)

5.277.s:
tena tāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ kṛtvā paścāttasyāḥ parigraham ..
gṛhyoktavidhinā cakre puraḥstho'pi pitāmahaḥ ..11..
5.277.d:
तेन तां ब्राह्मणीं कृत्वा पश्चात्तस्याः परिग्रहम् ..
गृह्योक्तविधिना चक्रे पुरःस्थोऽपि पितामहः ..11..
5.277.m: Having thus made her a brahmin woman, the grandfather, standing right before them, / then took her hand according to the rite prescribed in the domestic manuals. (11)

5.277.s:
patnīśālopaviṣṭāyāṃ tatastasyāṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
sāvitrī samanuprāptā devapatnībhirāvṛtā .. 12 ..
5.277.d:
पत्नीशालोपविष्टायां ततस्तस्यां द्विजोत्तमाः ..
सावित्री समनुप्राप्ता देवपत्नीभिरावृता .. 12 ..
5.277.m: Then, O best of twice-born, as she was seated in the wife's pavilion, / Sāvitrī arrived, surrounded by the wives of the gods. (12)

5.277.s:
tatastāṃ sā samālokya raśanāsamalaṃkṛtām ..
daurbhāgyaduḥkhamāpannā śaśāpa ca vidhiṃ tataḥ .. 13 ..
5.277.d:
ततस्तां सा समालोक्य रशनासमलंकृताम् ..
दौर्भाग्यदुःखमापन्ना शशाप च विधिं ततः .. 13 ..
5.277.m: Then, seeing her adorned with the girdle, / [Sāvitrī] fell into the distress of misfortune and then cursed Vidhi [Brahmā]: (13)

5.277.s:
.. sāvitryuvāca .. ..
yasmāttvayā parityaktā nirdoṣāhaṃ pitāmaha ..
pitāmaho'si me nūnamadyaprabhṛti saṃgame .. 14 ..
5.277.d:
.. सावित्र्युवाच .. ..
यस्मात्त्वया परित्यक्ता निर्दोषाहं पितामह ..
पितामहोऽसि मे नूनमद्यप्रभृति संगमे .. 14 ..
5.277.m:
Sāvitrī said:
Because I, who am innocent, have been abandoned by you, O Grandfather, / you shall indeed be my grandfather from this day forth in union! (14)

5.277.s:
manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavetkṛtyamanyanārīparigrahaḥ ..
etattvayā kṛtaṃ yasmānmā nuṣastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 15 ..
5.277.d:
मनुष्याणां भवेत्कृत्यमन्यनारीपरिग्रहः ..
एतत्त्वया कृतं यस्मान्मा नुषस्त्वं भविष्यसि .. 15 ..
5.277.m: The taking of another woman is the practice of mortals; / because this was done by you, you shall become a mortal, (15)

5.277.s: kāmārtaśca viśeṣeṇa mama vākyādasaṃśayam.. 16 ..
5.277.d: कामार्तश्च विशेषेण मम वाक्यादसंशयम्.. 16 ..
5.277.m: and afflicted by lust in particular, without a doubt, by my word! (16)

5.277.s:
evamuktvā tu sāvitrī tyaktvā taṃ yajñamaṃḍapam ..
gireḥ śikharamārūḍhā tapaścakre mahattataḥ .. 17 ..
5.277.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सावित्री त्यक्त्वा तं यज्ञमंडपम् ..
गिरेः शिखरमारूढा तपश्चक्रे महत्ततः .. 17 ..
5.277.m: Having spoken thus, Sāvitrī left that sacrificial pavilion, / climbed the peak of a mountain, and then performed great austerity. (17)

5.277.s:
pitāmaho'pi tacchāpāccārāyaṇaniveśane .
avatīrṇo dharāpṛṣṭhe kālena mahatā tataḥ .. 18 ..
5.277.d:
पितामहोऽपि तच्छापाच्चारायणनिवेशने .
अवतीर्णो धरापृष्ठे कालेन महता ततः .. 18 ..
5.277.m: The Grandfather too, because of that curse, descended onto the surface of the earth / in the dwelling of Cārāyaṇa after a long time. (18)

5.277.s:
sa yadā yauvanaṃ bheje mānuṣaṃ ca purā sthitaḥ ..
tathātathā ca tāpena kāmotthena prapīḍyate .. 19 .
5.277.d:
स यदा यौवनं भेजे मानुषं च पुरा स्थितः ..
तथातथा च तापेन कामोत्थेन प्रपीड्यते .. 19 .
5.277.m: When he attained mortal youth, having lived [there] previously, / he was tormented more and more by the fever arising from lust. (19)

5.277.s:
tato'sau vīkṣate nārīṃ kanyāṃ vātha tapasvinīm ..
avikalpamanā bheje rūpasaubhāgyagarvitaḥ .. 6.278.20 ..
5.277.d:
ततोऽसौ वीक्षते नारीं कन्यां वाथ तपस्विनीम् ..
अविकल्पमना भेजे रूपसौभाग्यगर्वितः .. 6.278.20 ..
5.277.m: Then, whenever he saw a woman, whether an unmarried girl or an ascetic woman, / his mind devoid of discretion, proud of his beauty and charm, he pursued her. (20)

5.277.s:
tatastaṃ byasanārtaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cārāyaṇo muniḥ ..
svayaṃ niḥsārayāmāsa prakopena nijāśramāt .. 21 ..
5.277.d:
ततस्तं ब्यसनार्तं च दृष्ट्वा चारायणो मुनिः ..
स्वयं निःसारयामास प्रकोपेन निजाश्रमात् .. 21 ..
5.277.m: Then, seeing him afflicted by this vice, the sage Cārāyaṇa / himself drove him out in great anger from his own hermitage. (21)

5.277.s:
sa ca pitrā parityakto bhramamāṇastatastataḥ ..
camatkārapuraṃ prāptaḥ śākalyo yatra tiṣṭhati .. 22 ..
5.277.d:
स च पित्रा परित्यक्तो भ्रममाणस्ततस्ततः ..
चमत्कारपुरं प्राप्तः शाकल्यो यत्र तिष्ठति .. 22 ..
5.277.m: Abandoned by his father, wandering here and there, / he reached Camatkārapura, where Śākalya resided— (22)

5.277.s:
nāmnā brāhmaṇaśārdūlo nāgaro vedapāragaḥ ..
vṛtaḥ śiṣya sahasreṇa vedavidyāṃ pracārayan.. 23 ..
5.277.d:
नाम्ना ब्राह्मणशार्दूलो नागरो वेदपारगः ..
वृतः शिष्य सहस्रेण वेदविद्यां प्रचारयन्.. 23 ..
5.277.m: an eminent brahmin by that name, an inhabitant of Nagara, completely versed in the Vedas, / surrounded by a thousand pupils, propagating the Vedic lore. (23)

5.277.s:
atha taṃ sa praṇamyoccaiḥ śiṣyatvaṃ samupāgataḥ ..
vedādhyayanasaṃpanno babhūvātha cirādapi .. 24 ..
5.277.d:
अथ तं स प्रणम्योच्चैः शिष्यत्वं समुपागतः ..
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नो बभूवाथ चिरादपि .. 24 ..
5.277.m: Then, having bowed deeply to him, he entered into discipleship, / and after a long time he became accomplished in the study of the Vedas. (24)

5.277.s:
etasminneva kāle nu ānartādhipatiḥ svayam ..
āgatastiṣṭhate yatra jalaśāyī hariḥ svayam .. 25 ..
5.277.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले नु आनर्ताधिपतिः स्वयम् ..
आगतस्तिष्ठते यत्र जलशायी हरिः स्वयम् .. 25 ..
5.277.m: At that very time, the king of Ānarta himself / came and stayed where Hari himself reclines upon the waters. (25)

5.277.s:
cāturmāsyavrataṃ tena gṛhītaṃ tatpurastadā ..
prārthitastu tato viprāḥ śākalyastaina bhūbhujā .. 26 ..
5.277.d:
चातुर्मास्यव्रतं तेन गृहीतं तत्पुरस्तदा ..
प्रार्थितस्तु ततो विप्राः शाकल्यस्तैन भूभुजा .. 26 ..
5.277.m: The vow of the four monsoon months was then undertaken by him before Him; / then, O brahmins, Śākalya was requested by that king: (26)

5.277.s:
śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ nityaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mamālaye ..
yāvattiṣṭhāmyahaṃ cātra prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti .. 27 ..
5.277.d:
शांतिकं पौष्टिकं नित्यं त्वया कार्यं ममालये ..
यावत्तिष्ठाम्यहं चात्र प्रसादः क्रियतामिति .. 27 ..
5.277.m: "A daily rite for peace and prosperity must be performed by you in my dwelling, / as long as I remain here; let this favor be granted." (27)

5.277.s:
bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā dākṣiṇyena dvijottamāḥ ..
ekaikaṃ preṣayāmāsa svaśiṣyaṃ tasya maṃdire .. 28 ..
5.277.d:
बाढमित्येव स प्रोक्त्वा दाक्षिण्येन द्विजोत्तमाः ..
एकैकं प्रेषयामास स्वशिष्यं तस्य मंदिरे .. 28 ..
5.277.m: Saying "So be it," out of courtesy, O best of twice-born, / he sent his pupils one by one to his palace. (28)

5.277.s:
sa śāṃtikaṃ vidhāyātha dattvāśīḥ pārthivasya ca ..
saṃprāpya dakṣiṇāṃ tasmātpunareti ca taṃ dvijam .. 29..
5.277.d:
स शांतिकं विधायाथ दत्त्वाशीः पार्थिवस्य च ..
संप्राप्य दक्षिणां तस्मात्पुनरेति च तं द्विजम् .. 29..
5.277.m: Having performed the pacification rite and given blessings to the king, / and having received a priestly gift from him, [each pupil] would return to that twice-born. (29)

5.277.s:
śākalyāya ca tāṃ dattvā dakṣiṇāṃ nijamaṃdire ..
jagāma nityamevaṃ hi vyavahāro vyavasthitaḥ .. 6.278.30 ..
5.277.d:
शाकल्याय च तां दत्त्वा दक्षिणां निजमंदिरे ..
जगाम नित्यमेवं हि व्यवहारो व्यवस्थितः .. 6.278.30 ..
5.277.m: And giving that priestly gift to Śākalya, he would go to his own room. / In this way the regular practice was maintained every day. (30)

5.277.s:
anyasminnahani prāpte śākalyena visarjitaḥ ..
śāṃtyarthaṃ yājñavalkyastu pārthivasyaniveśanam .. 31 ..
5.277.d:
अन्यस्मिन्नहनि प्राप्ते शाकल्येन विसर्जितः ..
शांत्यर्थं याज्ञवल्क्यस्तु पार्थिवस्यनिवेशनम् .. 31 ..
5.277.m: When another day arrived, Yājñavalkya was dispatched / by Śākalya to the palace of the king for the pacification rite. (31)

5.277.s:
tasya bhūpasya rūpāḍhayā maṃtharāsti vilāsinī ..
rātrau ca kāmitā tena kāmāḍhayena sukāminī .. 32 ..
5.277.d:
तस्य भूपस्य रूपाढया मंथरास्ति विलासिनी ..
रात्रौ च कामिता तेन कामाढयेन सुकामिनी .. 32 ..
5.277.m: That king had an amorous woman, rich in beauty, [named] Mantharā; / and during the night she, a passionate woman, was loved by him who was full of passion. (32)

5.277.s:
bhāvairvātsyāyanaproktaiḥ samāliṃganapūrvakaiḥ ..
sa tayā vividhaiḥ kṛtto mayūrapadakādibhiḥ ..
śarīre cādhare caiva tathā maṇipravālakaiḥ .. 33 ..
5.277.d:
भावैर्वात्स्यायनप्रोक्तैः समालिंगनपूर्वकैः ..
स तया विविधैः कृत्तो मयूरपदकादिभिः ..
शरीरे चाधरे चैव तथा मणिप्रवालकैः .. 33 ..
5.277.m: Through postures taught by Vātsyāyana, preceded by embraces, / he had been scratched by her with various marks, such as the peacock's foot, / on his body and his lower lip, and likewise with teeth-bites. (33)

5.277.s:
saṃprāpto'dhyayanārthāya yāvacchākalyasannidhau ..
tāvatsaṃpreṣitastena śāṃtyarthaṃ bhūpamaṃdire .. 34 ..
5.277.d:
संप्राप्तोऽध्ययनार्थाय यावच्छाकल्यसन्निधौ ..
तावत्संप्रेषितस्तेन शांत्यर्थं भूपमंदिरे .. 34 ..
5.277.m: As soon as he arrived in the presence of Śākalya for the purpose of study, / he was sent by him to the palace of the king for the pacification rite. (34)

5.277.s:
so'pi saṃpreṣitastena gatvā taṃ pārthivālayam ..
śāṃtikaṃ ca tataścakre yathoktavidhinā dvijāḥ .. 35 ..
5.277.d:
सोऽपि संप्रेषितस्तेन गत्वा तं पार्थिवालयम् ..
शांतिकं च ततश्चक्रे यथोक्तविधिना द्विजाः .. 35 ..
5.277.m: Dispatched by him, he went to the palace of that king / and then performed the pacification rite according to the prescribed rule, O twice-born. (35)

5.277.s:
śāṃtikasyāvasāne tu pragṛhya kalaśodakam ..
paṃcāṃgaiḥ kalpitaṃ rudraiḥ svayamevābhimaṃtritaiḥ .. 36 ..
5.277.d:
शांतिकस्यावसाने तु प्रगृह्य कलशोदकम् ..
पंचांगैः कल्पितं रुद्रैः स्वयमेवाभिमंत्रितैः .. 36 ..
5.277.m: At the conclusion of the pacification rite, he took up the water of the pitcher, / prepared with the five accessories and personally consecrated with the Rudra mantras; (36)

5.277.s:
sākṣataṃ sumanoyuktaṃ samādāya gatastataḥ ..
saṃtiṣṭhate nṛpo yatra ānarto tratasaṃyutaḥ .. 37 ..
5.277.d:
साक्षतं सुमनोयुक्तं समादाय गतस्ततः ..
संतिष्ठते नृपो यत्र आनर्तो त्रतसंयुतः .. 37 ..

Standing with palms joined, they spoke in haste to Śākalya: / “Send that disciple quickly; the king awaits on the path.”

Consenting with “So be it,” he went to the king’s dwelling / and performed the rite of pacification according to the prescribed rules.

5.277.m:
Sūta said: / Thus having studied the Vedas and having given the fee for a guru / to the sun, he returned again toward Camatkārapura. 112
Then, approaching Śākalya, [he said:] "You stood previously as my guru; / make a request, O fortunate one, and I will give you the fee for a guru. 113
An elder brother, a father, a mother, and likewise a guru, / even if they behave with hostility, O best of the twice-born, / are nevertheless to be honored by a man, without a doubt. 114
The four Vedas along with their limbs and secondary limbs have been studied by me; / they have been studied, and the meaning of all of them has been comprehended. 115
Therefore, say, O fortunate one, what fee shall I give you?" 116
Śākalya said: / "Those secrets of the Vedas which were told to you by the sun, 117
by which, when explained and recited, there would be destruction of sin— / recite those to me quickly; this is my fee for a guru." 118

Sūta said: / When it was agreed thus ('So be it') by those brahmins born in the four quarters, / Yājñavalkya was recognized in some way or another.
Then the lord of men [arrived] from Videha, for the sake of hearing [the teachings], / along with the earth-ruler named Ratna, to hear all the Upaniṣads.
And he, having also understood the māhātmya originating from the sun, / then established the sun in that place, O best of brahmins.
And that person who beholds it on a Sunday / is freed from sin committed over seven nights; there is no doubt about this.
All this māhātmya originating from the sun has been recounted to you. / A person who listens with devotion would obtain the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.
Whatever fruit [is obtained] by giving a gift at a solstice or by hearing [it] on Sunday, / he fully obtains that fruit having heard the supreme māhātmya.

यो नरः शृणुयाद्भक्त्या दिनानि च कियंति वै ..
सर्वार्थसिद्धो भवति य इमां पठते कथाम् . 9 ..
5.278.m: The man who would hear [it] with devotion even for a few days, / he who recites this narrative, has all his aims accomplished.

5.278.s:
putrārthī labhate putrāndhanārthī labhate dhanam ..
labhate patikāmā yā patiṃ kanyā manoramam .. 6.279.10 ..
5.278.d:
पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रान्धनार्थी लभते धनम् ..
लभते पतिकामा या पतिं कन्या मनोरमम् .. 6.279.10 ..
5.278.m: One desiring a son obtains sons; one desiring wealth obtains wealth; / a maiden desiring a husband obtains a pleasing husband.

5.278.s:
samāgamaṃ labhaṃte ca vāṃdhavāśca pravāsibhiḥ ..
skāṃdaṃ purāṇaṃ śrutvā tu pumānā pnoti vāṃchitam .. 11 ..
5.278.d:
समागमं लभंते च वांधवाश्च प्रवासिभिः ..
स्कांदं पुराणं श्रुत्वा तु पुमाना प्नोति वांछितम् .. 11 ..
5.278.m: And kinsmen obtain reunion with travelers abroad; / having heard the Skanda Purāṇa, a man obtains what he desires.

5.278.s:
śṛṇvataḥ paṭhataścaiva sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām ..
mahīṃ vijayate rājā śatrūṃścāpyadhitiṣṭhati .. 12 ..
5.278.d:
शृण्वतः पठतश्चैव सर्वकामप्रदं नृणाम् ..
महीं विजयते राजा शत्रूंश्चाप्यधितिष्ठति .. 12 ..
5.278.m: For men who listen and recite, it grants all desires; / a king conquers the earth and triumphs over enemies.

5.278.s:
puṇyaṃ śrutvā purāṇaṃ vai dīrghamā yuśca viṃdati ..
vedavicca bhavedvipraḥ kṣatriyo rājyamāpnuyāt .. 13 ..
5.278.d:
पुण्यं श्रुत्वा पुराणं वै दीर्घमा युश्च विंदति ..
वेदविच्च भवेद्विप्रः क्षत्रियो राज्यमाप्नुयात् .. 13 ..
5.278.m: Having heard this sacred Purāṇa, one finds a long life; / a brahmin becomes a knower of the Veda, a kṣatriya attains a kingdom,

5.278.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā vaiśyaḥ śūdraḥ sukhamavāpnuyāt ..
yaḥ ślokapādaṃ śṛṇuyādviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati .. 14 ..
5.278.d:
धनं धान्यं तथा वैश्यः शूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात् ..
यः श्लोकपादं शृणुयाद्विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति .. 14 ..
5.278.m: a vaiśya [attains] wealth and grain, and a śūdra attains happiness; / he who hears even a quarter of a verse goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

5.278.s:
śrutvā purāṇametaddhi vācakaṃ yastu pūjayet ..
tena brahmā ca viṣṇuśca rudraścaiva prapūjitaḥ .. 15 ..
5.278.d:
श्रुत्वा पुराणमेतद्धि वाचकं यस्तु पूजयेत् ..
तेन ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्चैव प्रपूजितः .. 15 ..
5.278.m: Having heard this Purāṇa, he who worships the narrator, / by him Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra have been worshiped.

5.278.s:
ekamapyakṣaraṃ yastu guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet..
pṛthivyā nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā hyanṛṇī bhavet ..16..
5.278.d:
एकमप्यक्षरं यस्तु गुरुः शिष्ये निवेदयेत्..
पृथिव्या नास्ति तद्द्रव्यं यद्दत्त्वा ह्यनृणी भवेत् ..16..
5.278.m: Whatever single syllable a guru may impart to a disciple, / there is no object on earth by giving which one would become free from debt [to him].

5.278.s:
ataḥ saṃpūjanīyastu vyāsaḥ śāstropadeśakaḥ ..
gobhūhiraṇyavastrādyairbhojanaiḥ sārva kāmikaiḥ ..17..
5.278.d:
अतः संपूजनीयस्तु व्यासः शास्त्रोपदेशकः ..
गोभूहिरण्यवस्त्राद्यैर्भोजनैः सार्व कामिकैः ..17..
5.278.m: Therefore, the reciter, the instructor of the scripture, should be fully honored / with cows, land, gold, garments, and all kinds of desirable foods.

5.278.s:
ya evaṃ bhaktiyuktastu śrutvā śāstramanutamam ..
pūjayedupadeṣṭāraṃ sa śaivaṃ padamāpnuyāt .. 18 ..
5.278.d:
य एवं भक्तियुक्तस्तु श्रुत्वा शास्त्रमनुतमम् ..
पूजयेदुपदेष्टारं स शैवं पदमाप्नुयात् .. 18 ..
5.278.m: He who, endowed with devotion, having heard this supreme scripture, / worships the teacher, attains the realm of Śiva.

5.278.s:
purāṇaśravaṇādeva anekabhavasaṃcitam ..
pāpaṃ praśamamāyāti sarvatīrthaphalaṃ labhet ..19..
5.278.d:
पुराणश्रवणादेव अनेकभवसंचितम् ..
पापं प्रशममायाति सर्वतीर्थफलं लभेत् ..19..
5.278.m: Just by hearing the Purāṇa, the sin accumulated over many births / comes to cessation, and one obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.

5.278.s:
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye purāṇaśravaṇamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonāśītyuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..279.. ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇe ṣaṣṭhaṃ nāgarakhaṇḍaṃ samāptam .. 6 ..
5.278.d:
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पुराणश्रवणमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनाशीत्युत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..279.. ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराणे षष्ठं नागरखण्डं समाप्तम् .. 6 ..
5.278.m:
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Hearing the Purāṇa, in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Holy Hāṭakeśvara,' in the sixth [section], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the great Purāṇa of Skanda consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Thus ends the sixth [section], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the great Purāṇa of Skanda. 6.
